chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Hamza, raising it, said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) stood at the door of Ibn Abu Mueet, and the camels used to stand therein, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O group of middlemen! Lessen the oaths, for (although) these are more profitable for the price, (but) are (eventually) destructive for the profits'.
ai.seo_question: What is the economic and spiritual impact of using oaths in trade according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) direct engagement with the commercial practices of his time, specifically targeting the Samsara (brokers) who used excessive oaths to inflate prices. The phrase 'manfaqah lil-silahah, mahiqah lil-ribh' illustrates the theological and economic paradox where the initial boost in sales value is ultimately offset by the erosion of profit through divine curse or loss of trust. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating spiritual integrity with economic transactions, viewing commercial honesty as a form of worship.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Aban Bin Taghlub, from Abu Hamza, raising it, said,

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> stood at the door of Ibn Abu Mueet, and the camels used to stand therein, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O group of middlemen! Lessen the oaths, for (although) these are more profitable for the price, (but) are (eventually) destructive for the profits’.
en.sarwar: 2. Through the same chain of narrators as the previous one is the following Hadith from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Aban ibn Taghlib from abu Hamzah in a marfu’ manner’ has said, the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once stood on the house of ibn abu Mu‘ayt where camel men stayed, and said, ‘O middlemen people, you must reduce swearing; it makes a merchandise easily marketable but destroys the profit.’”
